w:r.w:t: Complete Trading Manual — Bull & Recovery Markets
NSE/India Optimised | Powered by Weinstein Stage Analysis, Wyckoff Methodology & Minervini VCP

Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis is the foundational framework of the Commander Suite. Published in 'Secrets For Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets' (1988), Weinstein's methodology classifies every stock into one of four stages based on the relationship between price and the 30-week moving average (30WMA).

The core premise is simple yet powerful: stocks spend their time moving through predictable cycles. Understanding which stage a stock is in — and acting accordingly — is the single most important edge a trader can have.
Only buy stocks in Stage 2. Never buy Stage 4. Never average down in a declining position.
Duration guide: Stage 1 lasts weeks to months; Stage 2 lasts months to years; Stage 3 lasts weeks; Stage 4 lasts months.

Richard Wyckoff observed that markets move in cycles driven by institutional 'Composite Man' activity — large operators who accumulate positions during periods of apparent weakness and distribute during strength. Understanding these cycles allows traders to align with institutional order flow.
Accumulation: Institutional buying absorbs supply. Price moves sideways with declining volume. The public is bearish.
Markup: Supply exhausted; demand dominates. Price rises. This is Weinstein Stage 2.
Distribution: Institutions sell into public buying at highs. Price moves sideways with high, erratic volume.
Markdown: Supply dominates. Price declines. This is Weinstein Stage 4.

The Composite Man concept: Wyckoff's 'Composite Man' is a conceptual large operator who plans, executes and concludes campaigns across time. Recognising his 'footprints' — Springs, Upthrusts, SOS, SOW events — gives you a directional edge before the crowd realises what is happening.

Integration with Weinstein: Accumulation events (SC, ST, Spring, LPS) confirm Stage 1 base quality. SOS confirms Stage 2 entry. Distribution events (BC, UT, SOW, LPSY) confirm Stage 3 exit timing. The Weinstein Wyckoff Phases v1.0 Pine script automates detection of all 13 events.

Mark Minervini's Volatility Contraction Pattern identifies the final tightening phase before a major breakout. Within a Stage 2 base, price action contracts in both amplitude and volume, creating a series of smaller and smaller swings — like a coiling spring storing energy.

VCP structure: The base typically has 2-4 contractions. Each swing tightens by at least 30-50%. Volume dries up significantly in the final contraction. The pivot point is the highest point of the tightest contraction.
Entry at the pivot: Price closes above the pivot point on volume 1.5x or more above the 50-day average. This confirms institutional demand is absorbing remaining supply.

Weinstein Stage Analysis and Wyckoff methodology apply universally across markets including Indian equities. NSE/BSE present unique characteristics worth understanding:

BSE 500 as the primary universe: The Commander Suite screens BSE 500 stocks — India's broadest large/mid-cap index capturing ~90% of market capitalisation. Sufficient liquidity and coverage for swing and positional strategies.

FII/DII Flow Importance: Foreign Institutional Investors (FII) and Domestic Institutional Investors (DII) together represent 40-50% of NSE daily turnover. Net FII buying is the dominant driver of Stage 2 breakouts in quality large-caps. Monitor daily via the MACRO RADAR page.
India VIX as fear gauge: India VIX above 20 signals elevated uncertainty. Reduce all position sizes by 50% when VIX exceeds 20. VIX above 25 is a signal to step to cash entirely.

India 10Y yield context: Rising yield (above 7.5%) increases cost of capital and typically headwinds high-PE growth stocks. Prefer value and dividend-paying Stage 2 stocks in rising yield environments.

USD/INR dynamics: Rupee weakening (USDINR rising) reduces FII equity flows and typically coincides with market corrections. A rising INR (strengthening) is broadly positive for FII flows and market sentiment.

Geopolitical correction phase 2025+: The Recovery Strategy was specifically designed for the India market correction that began in late 2024 — a geo-political event-driven decline rather than a fundamental bear market, making recovery strategies particularly applicable.

The Commander Platform is a Python/Streamlit web application (weinstein_commander_web_v4.0.py) providing a comprehensive dashboard for NSE India market analysis, integrating live data, AI-generated reports, and breadth analytics.
The platform is built in four layers:
Layer 1: Data Hub (market_data_hub.py) — NSE, Dhan API, yfinance, NSEPython. Handles all market data fetching with TTL caching.
Layer 2: Analysis Engine (breadth_engine.py) — Stage classification, SMA breadth calculations, sector analysis, A/D ratio.
Layer 3: AI Reporter (gemini_reporter.py) — Gemini 2.0 Flash, pre/post market briefs generation with smart caching.
Layer 4: Web UI (weinstein_commander_web_v4.0.py) — Streamlit, all dashboard pages.
Centralized market data hub covering global indices, commodities, currencies, bonds, India VIX, FII/DII flows, NSE breadth, options chain (PCR/Max Pain), and corporate actions.

Stage classification: A stock is classified Stage 2 when: (1) price above SMA200, AND (2) SMA200 slope is positive over last 20 days. This produces a simplified but robust Stage 2 identification without requiring the full Weinstein state machine.
load_universe_symbols(): Tries nifty500_symbols.json first; falls back to the hardcoded Nifty 50 list if file not found. The JSON file should contain 500 Yahoo Finance tickers (e.g. 'RELIANCE.NS').

Cache logic: Strips volatile fields (generated_at, fetched_at, timestamp, calculated_at) before hashing. Same market data = same cache key = no duplicate API calls. TTL = 10 minutes.
Rate limit handling: 429 errors trigger exponential backoff retry — 60 seconds wait on first retry, 120 seconds on second retry.

How to interpret: Stage 2 percentage above 35% = bull market confirmed. Stage 4 percentage above 40% = bear market. Stage 1 exceeding Stage 4 = base-building phase (recovery). Equal spread = transitional market.
Action: Check Stage Map every Sunday before the trading week begins. A week-on-week drop in Stage 2 percentage is an early warning of regime change.
All four conditions must be satisfied before activating the bull trading plan:
Stage Map: Stage 2 stocks > Stage 4 stocks
Trend: Nifty above its own 30-week MA (30WMA rising)
FII: Net positive over rolling 5 trading days
If any of these four conditions fail, reduce to recovery mode parameters (Part 4) or step to cash entirely.
Step-by-step identification of a valid Stage 2 breakout setup:
Stock must be in Stage 2: Price above rising 30-week MA, 30WMA itself rising
Mansfield RS Line > 0 and rising: Stock is outperforming Nifty on a 26-week rolling basis
Base formed: At least 6-8 weeks of sideways/tight action after a prior advance
VCP visible: Contracting volatility (ATR shrinking), declining volume in the base
Pivot point identified: Highest point of the tightest part of the base
Entry trigger: Close above pivot point on volume greater than 1.5x the 20-day average
The strongest setups have Mansfield RS Line already breaking to new highs before the price pivot breaks — the RS line leading price is an early institutional accumulation signal.
Buy on pivot breakout: Close above pivot point, confirmed at market close
Alternative: Use a buy-stop order placed 0.5% above the pivot high for automated entry
Do not chase: Never buy more than 3% above the pivot point — the edge degrades rapidly above that level
Preferred timing: 9:45-10:30 AM IST after gap-up confirmation on the opening 15-min candle
Gap-up entries: Require the close to be in the top 40% of the gap bar's range (anti-algo gap-and-crap filter)
Initial stop: Below the base low OR 7-8% below entry, whichever is tighter
The stop must be pre-planned before entry — never decide after entering
Never widen the stop after entry. If the stop is hit, exit and reassess.
Move stop to breakeven after +15% gain from entry
Minimum stop distance: 3% below entry. Stops closer than 3% invite noise stops in NSE-listed stocks.
A stop loss is not a prediction — it is a pre-agreed budget. Once set, it does not move wider.
Formula: Position Size (shares) = (Account Value x Risk %) / (Entry Price - Stop Price)
Maximum 6% total portfolio heat (sum of all open position risks simultaneously)
Maximum 4 positions in the same sector at any time
Kelly Fraction boost: When Stage 2 + RS positive + Volume above average all align, size can scale up to 1.25% risk. Scale down to 0.75% in weak conditions (use_kelly = true in Strategy v4.51).
Divide every position into three tranches at entry. Each tranche has a pre-defined exit rule:
T1 — 40% of position: Sell at +20-25% gain. Action: Move remaining stop to breakeven.
T2 — 40% of position: Sell at +40-50% gain. Action: Trail remaining 20% with 30WMA.
T3 — 20% of position: Hold until Stage 3 distribution signal or close below 30WMA on high volume.
The tranche system lets you bank real profits at reasonable targets while still participating in the rare 100%+ winners that define bull market performance.
Exit rules in order of priority:
Hard stop hit: Price closes below your pre-set stop loss — exit immediately at open next day
Stage 3 distribution: Climax top volume, high-volume reversal at highs, Wyckoff BC/UT event detected
30WMA breach: Price closes below the 30-week moving average on above-average volume
Mansfield RS below 0: Stock underperforming Nifty on a weekly basis — institutional selling
Wyckoff SOW or LPSY detected by the Pine script — see Appendix A for event definitions
Breadth deterioration: % stocks above SMA200 drops more than 10 percentage points in a single week

A recovery market is the transitional period following a bear market bottom. It is characterised by selective institutional accumulation in fundamentally strong stocks while broader market conditions remain challenging.
Post-bear market bottoming process: The market has made a significant low and is attempting to establish a base
Mixed breadth: Some sectors recovering, others still declining — not a uniform bull
Selective institutional accumulation: FII buying visible in specific sectors/stocks while others remain under pressure
Stage Map signal: Stage 1 percentage exceeding Stage 4 percentage — stocks are basing, not declining
Recovery markets are higher-risk, lower-certainty environments. The potential reward justifies participation only with significantly reduced position sizes and faster profit-taking.
ALL of the following conditions must be simultaneously true before activating any recovery trade:
% stocks above SMA50 > 35% (short-term momentum returning to the market)
% stocks above SMA200 > 25% (long-term trend improvement beginning)
Stage Map: Stage 1 + Stage 2 combined exceeds 50% of all stocks
FII: Net positive at least 3 of the last 5 trading days
India VIX < 22 (fear subsiding — above 22 means institutions are still risk-off)
The regime gate is binary. If any single condition fails, NO new recovery entries. Wait for all five conditions to align.

Technical implementation: The Weinstein Recovery Strategy v1.1 Pine script checks CNX500 SMA50 < SMA200 (market in recovery mode) OR the individual stock has corrected >= 10% from its 52W high. This is the Pine-level equivalent of the regime gate.

The Recovery Fundamental Filter (RFF) prevents buying fundamentally weak stocks on technical bounces. Recovery rallies in weak businesses are dangerous — they look identical to genuine turnarounds until they fail.
RFF checks 6 criteria (from the Pine script implementation):
Net Income > 0 (profitable on TTM basis — NI check via request.financial)
Free Cash Flow > 0 (OCF minus |CapEx| positive — actual cash generation, not accounting profit)
Interest Coverage Ratio > 2.0 (EBITDA / Interest Expense — can service debt comfortably)
Debt/Equity < 2.0 (leverage within acceptable bounds for a recovery candidate)
Current Ratio > 1.0 (Current Assets / Current Liabilities — short-term liquidity)
Return on Assets > 5% (Net Income / Total Assets x 100 — capital efficiency)
Minimum score: Default rff_min_score = 3 (3 of 6 must pass). Set to 0 to disable. Set to 6 for strictest screening.
Do not override the RFF filter just because a stock has a 'good story'. The filter exists precisely to prevent narrative-driven buying of fundamentally impaired businesses.
4.4 T1 Asymmetry — Recovery vs Bull Comparison

Recovery mode uses significantly tighter profit targets and smaller position sizes than bull mode. Recovery rallies frequently reverse — taking profits faster is not timid, it is statistically correct.
Recovery rallies often stall at key resistance
SMA200 / 52W High acts as strong resistance
Tighter stop = faster exit if thesis fails
Recovery bases take longer to develop
The Recovery Strategy v1.1 implements three distinct entry edges:
Designed to catch the first bounce from a panic low. Requires all four pillars:
Pillar 1 — Stretch: Price is >= 15% below SMA200 (deeply discounted from fair value)
Pillar 2 — Washout: RSI14 < 30 AND RSI3 < 15 (multi-timeframe oversold confirmation)
Pillar 3 — Climax Volume: Volume >= 2.5x 50-bar average on a bearish bar or wide-range bar (panic capitulation)
Pillar 4 — Turn: Within 10 bars of climax, a green candle closing in top 40% of range, breaking prior bar's high
Stop: Climax zone low minus 0.5x ATR. T1: EMA20 (30% partial). T2: SMA200 (25% partial).
Targets stocks that held up relative to the broader market during the correction — institutional favourites.
Positive Mansfield RS vs CNX500 during the correction period
Recovery state: Price above SMA50 (NOTE: SMA50 < SMA200 gate was removed in v1.1 — RS survivors often held so well they never had a death cross)
Breakout above 20-day high on volume > 1.5x 50-bar average
Stop: 10-bar structural low minus 0.2x ATR. T1: 2.5R (30% partial). T2: 52W High (25% partial). Trail: Chandelier ratchet.
REV-EARLY: Early Bird (VCP near Golden Cross)
Targets emerging leaders approaching a Stage 1 to Stage 2 transition:
SMA50 within 5% of SMA200 (near_gc_pct = 5.0) or already crossed above
Minervini trend structure: Close > SMA50 > SMA150, and SMA50 > SMA200 x 0.95
VCP tightness: ATR(10) < SMA50(ATR10) x 1.5 AND VWMA(volume, 5) < SMA(volume, 50)
Pivot breakout: Close above 15-bar high on volume > 1.5x average
Stop: 10-bar structural low minus 0.2x ATR. T1: 2.5R. T2: 52W High. Trail: Chandelier ratchet.
Exit immediately if the regime gate turns off (breadth drops below threshold mid-trade)
Exit if stock returns to Stage 4 (close below declining 30WMA)
Take T1 faster than bull mode — at 10-15% rather than waiting for 20%+
Do not average down on recovery trades. If stopped out, wait for a new valid signal.
REV-CB specific: Exit if close drops below SMA50 ('50MA Fail' exit). CB Time Stop: if T1 not reached within 10 days, exit.
REV-RS/EARLY specific: Stage 4 macro exit activates if weekly stage drops to 4. Positional time-decay: exit if open >= 40 days (8 weeks x 5) with unrealised R < 0.5 and no breakeven achieved.

Purpose: Full-automation backtesting engine for the bull market playbook. Implements 6 entry edges across two strategy modes (Positional and Swing), with adaptive Chandelier Exit trailing stops, Kelly Fraction sizing, and a live Risk Allocator table.

POS-BO (Stage 2 Breakout) requires: Stage 2 confirmed on weekly chart, Mansfield RS > 0 (weekly), breakout above bo_len-day high on volume > 1.5x average, trend_template_ok (within 25% of 52W high AND > 30% above 52W low), sector in Stage 1 or 2, macro edge conditions met (Vol Shelf active).

Purpose: Smart Money Concepts overlay implementing Order Blocks, Fair Value Gaps (FVG), Break of Structure (BOS) / Change of Character (CHoCH), and Liquidity Sweeps.
Bullish Order Block: Last bearish candle before a bullish BOS. Price tends to react when it returns to this zone as institutions have buy orders here.
Bearish Order Block: Last bullish candle before a bearish BOS. Acts as supply zone on retest.
Bullish FVG: high[2] < low[0] — gap acts as support on first retest. Auto-mitigated when price closes through.
Bearish FVG: low[2] > high[0] — gap acts as resistance on retest. Auto-mitigated on close above.
BOS (Break of Structure): Price breaks a prior confirmed swing high/low — continuation signal.
CHoCH (Change of Character): First BOS in the opposite direction of prevailing structure — potential reversal.
Liquidity Sweep: Price briefly exceeds prior swing but closes back inside — typical institutional stop-hunt before reversal.
ob_len: 5 bars (swing length for order block detection)
ob_mitigated: false (remove OBs when price closes through)
fvg_min_pct: 0.05% (minimum gap size to qualify as FVG)
bos_len: 10 bars (swing length for BOS detection)
liq_len: 10 bars (swing length for liquidity sweep detection)

Formula: qty_by_risk = floor(risk_amount / stop_distance / multiplier). qty_by_capital = floor(allocation_per_trade / entry_price / multiplier). final_qty = min(qty_by_risk, qty_by_capital). Capped allocation triggers warning label.

Purpose: Portfolio-level Chandelier Exit trailing stop. Applies the CE algorithm to the current chart symbol, providing a dynamic stop that ratchets upward in Stage 2. Includes a server-side alert that fires when price closes below the CE stop.

Logic: raw_long_stop = highest(high, ce_length) - ATR(atr_length) x ce_mult. Ratchet rule: if yesterday's close was above yesterday's stop, the stop is max(raw_long_stop, prior_stop) — it only moves up. If yesterday's close was below yesterday's stop, it resets to raw_long_stop.

Visual: Green line when close above stop (Stage 2 intact), red when below. EMA20 shown as thin blue reference. Alert condition: ta.crossunder(close, trailing_stop) — triggers SELL ALERT message with ticker and price.
Use case: Apply to each portfolio position. When the green CE line turns red on a close, it is an exit signal. The alert automates notification so you do not need to watch the chart continuously.

Review FII/DII overnight: note net direction and magnitude. Three consecutive negative FII days = avoid aggressive entries.

Never risk more than 1% of your total account on any single trade. This is the foundational rule of the Commander Suite and applies in all market conditions. In recovery mode, the default is 0.5-0.75%.
If entry = Rs 500 and stop = Rs 465 (7% stop), risk per share = Rs 35
Total position value = 286 x Rs 500 = Rs 1,43,000 (14.3% of capital)

The 1% rule means you can sustain 50 consecutive losing trades before losing half your capital — a scenario that is statistically impossible with proper setups. This psychological safety net is essential for executing plans without fear.
Position Size (shares) = (Account Value x Risk %) / (Entry Price - Stop Price)
Capped by: Max Allocation per Trade / Entry Price
Portfolio heat is the total simultaneous risk across all open positions — the sum of (Entry - Stop) x Shares for every active trade.
Track using the Portfolio Risk Allocator v6.1 Pine script on each open position
If total heat approaches the maximum: take profits on profitable positions rather than opening new ones
Never open a new position that would breach the maximum heat rule
After a 3-trade losing streak, halve position sizes until 2 consecutive winners restore confidence
1R = initial risk (distance from entry to stop price). Every trade outcome is measured in multiples of R:
A 2R win = profit of twice the initial risk
A 0.5R loss = stopped out at half the initial stop distance
Expectancy formula: E = (Win% x Avg Win R) - (Loss% x Avg Loss R)
Example: 50% win rate, average win 2R, average loss 1R = (0.5 x 2) - (0.5 x 1) = +0.5R per trade.
With Rs 10,000 risk per trade (1% of Rs 10L account), +0.5R expectancy = +Rs 5,000 expected per trade.
Track your actual R-multiples in a trading journal. Most traders discover their true expectancy is lower than expected, which helps identify specific areas for improvement.
Reduce all new position sizes by 50% until equity recovers above -3%
Stop all new entries. Manage existing positions only. Review methodology.
Full stop on new entries. Review every open position for continued validity.
Exit all positions. Reset to paper trading for minimum 2 weeks.
Maximum 3 stocks from the same sector open simultaneously — correlations exceed 0.8 in sector rallies
After a sector position is stopped out, wait 5 trading days before re-entering that sector
Use BREADTH → Sectors tab to avoid adding to sectors with declining SMA150 slope
Maximum 2 positions correlated to the same macro theme (e.g. both crude oil plays)

Pine script Stage detection logic (Dashboard v62.0 / Strategy v4.51): Stage 2 requires rising w_slope (> dynamic threshold) AND close above SMA150.
